# nginx — 2025 high-value CVEs (CVSS>=7, CISA KEV, Exploit-DB, or SSVC exploitation active/poc)

Full records for all 18 nginx CVEs of 2025 are in `data/cve/vendors/nginx/2025.jsonl`.

### CVE-2025-1097 — ingress-nginx controller - configuration injection via unsanitized auth-tls-match-cn annotation
- Assigner: kubernetes | Published: 2025-03-24 | Updated: 2026-02-26 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-20 CWE-20 Improper Input Validation
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- Exploit-DB 52475: Ingress-NGINX Admission Controller v1.11.1 - FD Injection to RCE (remote/multiple, 2026-02-04, verified=0)

A security issue was discovered in  ingress-nginx https://github.com/kubernetes/ingress-nginx  where the `auth-tls-match-cn` Ingress annotation can be used to inject configuration into nginx. This can lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the ingress-nginx controller, and disclosure of Secrets accessible to the controller. (Note that in the default installation, the controller can access all Secrets cluster-wide.)

Affected:
- kubernetes / ingress-nginx: affected 0 <=1.11.4 (semver); affected 1.12.0

Credits: Nir Ohfeld; Ronen Shustin; Sagi Tzadik; Hillai Ben Sasson

References:
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/131007
- https://security.netapp.com/advisory/ntap-20250328-0008/
- https://www.exploit-db.com/exploits/52475

### CVE-2025-1974 — ingress-nginx admission controller RCE escalation
- Assigner: kubernetes | Published: 2025-03-24 | Updated: 2026-02-26 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: CWE-653 CWE-653 Improper Isolation or Compartmentalization
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total
- Exploit-DB 52338: Ingress-NGINX 4.11.0 - Remote Code Execution (RCE) (remote/multiple, 2025-06-20, verified=1)
- Exploit-DB 52475: Ingress-NGINX Admission Controller v1.11.1 - FD Injection to RCE (remote/multiple, 2026-02-04, verified=0)

A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where under certain conditions, an unauthenticated attacker with access to the pod network can achieve arbitrary code execution in the context of the ingress-nginx controller. This can lead to disclosure of Secrets accessible to the controller. (Note that in the default installation, the controller can access all Secrets cluster-wide.)

**workarounds:** Before applying the patch, this issue can be mitigated by disabling the Validating Admission Controller functionality of ingress-nginx.

Affected:
- kubernetes / ingress-nginx: affected 0 <=1.11.4 (semver); affected 1.12.0

Credits: Nir Ohfeld; Ronen Shustin; Sagi Tzadik; Hillai Ben Sasson

References:

- https://github.com/B1ack4sh/Blackash-CVE-2025-1974
- https://www.exploit-db.com/exploits/52475

### CVE-2025-6213 — Nginx Cache Purge Preload <= 2.1.1 - Authenticated (Administrator+) Remote Code Execution
- Assigner: Wordfence | Published: 2025-07-22 | Updated: 2026-04-08 | Max CVSS: 7.2
- CWE: CWE-94 CWE-94 Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.2 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

The Nginx Cache Purge Preload plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and including, 2.1.1 via the 'nppp_preload_cache_on_update' function. This is due to insufficient sanitization of the $_SERVER['HTTP_REFERERER'] parameter passed from the 'nppp_handle_fastcgi_cache_actions_admin_bar' function. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Administrator-level access and above, to execute code on the server.

Affected:
- psauxit / Nginx Cache Purge Preload: affected 0 <=2.1.1 (semver)

Credits: cynau1t

References:
- https://www.wordfence.com/threat-intel/vulnerabilities/id/bbe8c101-5e0a-4ba7-8ff7-4c8ed01e9ef5?source=cve
- https://wordpress.org/plugins/fastcgi-cache-purge-and-preload-nginx/
- https://github.com/psaux-it/nginx-fastcgi-cache-purge-and-preload
- https://plugins.trac.wordpress.org/changeset?sfp_email=&sfph_mail=&reponame=&old=3332176%40fastcgi-cache-purge-and-preload-nginx&new=3332176%40fastcgi-cache-purge-and-preload-nginx&sfp_email=&sfph_mail=#file15

### CVE-2025-56005
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2026-01-20 | Updated: 2026-09-17 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: n/a; CWE-502 CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data; CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

An undocumented and unsafe feature in the PLY (Python Lex-Yacc) library 3.11 allows Remote Code Execution (RCE) via the `picklefile` parameter in the `yacc()` function. This parameter accepts a `.pkl` file that is deserialized with `pickle.load()` without validation. Because `pickle` allows execution of embedded code via `__reduce__()`, an attacker can achieve code execution by passing a malicious pickle file. The parameter is not mentioned in official documentation or the GitHub repository, yet it is active in the PyPI version. This introduces a stealthy backdoor and persistence risk. NOTE: A third-party states that this vulnerability should be rejected because the proof of concept does not demonstrate arbitrary code execution and fails to complete successfully.
